novelty_basis: S. Markovski, D. Gligoroski, V. Bakeva, Quasigroup string processing, Part 1, Contributions, Sec. Math. Tech. Sci., MANU (1999) - the E- and D-transformations with the same leader are mutually inverse permutations of strings (as cited in US patent 8041031, https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/8041031, and in Markovski-Bakeva, Quasigroup String Processing Part 4, https://www.academia.edu/115482463/Quasigroup_String_Processing_Part_4).
proof_check: Lean 4 + Mathlib (eT_injective, eT_length; standard axioms only) plus the finite-cardinality step (written proof, proofs/paper/C18.md Theorem 1); d(e(X)) = X for all seven quasigroups (EXP-C18-01)
statement: For every quasigroup Q, leader l and length n, the e-transformation e_l is a bijection of Q^n, inverted by the d-transformation a_i = b_(i-1) \ b_i; hence every composition of forward and reversed e-transformations is a bijection of Q^n.
title: e-transformations are bijections of strings of fixed length
